problems.title: Umbra and penumbra
problems.statement: As you know, on clear sunny days, objects usually give rise to umbras and penumbras. Nowadays, the angle of the ecliptic plane to the celestial equator is $\varepsilon_0=23^\circ26.2'$ and is reduced by about $\upsilon=0.78'$ per century. Calculate in what century begins the period or in what century the period has ended when from the exactly vertical column located in Ashulia

problems.title: Star setting
problems.statement: The Bengal Tiger likes to observe stars. According to his calculations, some star will rise today at $19^{\rm h}45^{\rm m}$ and will culminate at $21^{\rm h}49^{\rm m}$. At what time yesterday did the star set? The refraction and horizon lowering can be disregarded. The solution has to include an artistic picture with an image of the Bengal Tiger-astronomer observing the star.

solution.incompleteReason: No official solutions are present in the inspected APAO 2015 archive.

problems.title: Lunokhod
problems.statement: While the Bengal Tiger holds astronomical observations near Dhaka, the White Bear traveled to the Moon. Possessing Lunokhod (lunar rover), he is moving along the lunar equator, with the Sun being observed at the horizon during all the way. Calculate the speed of Lunokhod. The solution has to include an artistic picture with an image of the Bear-astronomer riding on Lunokhod and observing the Sun.

solution.incompleteReason: No official solutions are present in the inspected APAO 2015 archive.

problems.title: Distance between stars
problems.statement: In our region of the Galaxy the stellar matter density is about $1.5\cdot10^{29}$ kg per cubic parsec. Assuming the stars are of solar type, estimate the average distance between the stars. Draw a picture explaining your solution.

problems.title: M32
problems.statement: There are about 250 million stars in the elliptical galaxy M32 (a satellite of the Andromeda galaxy). The visual magnitude of this galaxy is 9 mag. Assuming luminosities of all the stars is equal, what is the visual magnitude of one star in this galaxy?
